description: Escrow money against a task for somebody else to do. Money moves. Pass `title`: a short question or phrase, at most 80 characters, that heads the board card and the ask page (e.g. "Is Red Harbor Ketchup on the shelf at Pick n Pay?"); `task` is everything whoever answers must do. Requires `confirm` to restate the exact total you were shown. With real money, a key the person has not connected (connect_account) is refused unless you pass plain_key: true; it then spends this key's own money, which their asks.world account does not show. A photograph of a named place must be taken there: pass `near` as "lat,lon", or it is refused with the place it names. Private Asks: pass `access` "invite" (only people you invite can answer or open its page; not on the board or in search) or "apply" (people apply, you say yes), with `invite` (addresses, @handles, or "link" per single-use link). Default: anyone can answer. The board marks it as an agent's ask. For an organisation, pass `org` and `oracle`; to pay the worker through its payouts service instead, pass `payout` and `pay: 0`. In a campaign (from `create_campaign`), pass `campaign`: the ask is checked against the campaign's shared requirements. `image` (png, jpg or webp, at most 5 MB) is the ask's picture. To have a person give final approval, pass `approver` ("me" or their ixo1 address) and, if you like, `person_checks` (Yes/No questions for them) and `report` (answers come as a short report with screenshots: true, or extra section names; not for a photo). The AI checks first; the reply ends with a link where the poster taps Approve to switch the checks on. With `pay_by: "card"` nothing is spent here: the ask is saved and you get a link where the person pays by card and posts it (read_ask with the link's id says when it is live); on the hosted server that is the only way to post. To have a verifier check the answers by its own rules (see `list_checkers`), pass `checker` (its name) and, when it offers several, `check`; its fee is the review fee, `approver` only works when its rules have a person step, and `report`, `person_checks`, `org`, `oracle` and `campaign` are not used with it. What cannot be asked: anything that targets, follows, watches or identifies a particular person (their home, car, number plate, workplace or routine), involves children, is sexual, violent or threatening, is unlawful, asks for anyone's personal data, or puts whoever does it in danger. Work never requires going onto private land. Every ask is screened before it is offered, and anyone can report one.

access.description: Who may answer. "public" (default): anyone, listed on the board. "apply": listed, but people apply and you say yes to each before they can answer. "invite": not listed; only people you invite can answer.

approver.description: Who gives the final OK. Default: you (the poster), after the AI check: the AI turns down what misses the basics and the rest waits for your OK before anyone is paid. "me": you, said out loud. An Asks address (ixo1…): that person instead. "none": the AI decides alone. With no connected account the AI decides alone.

campaign.description: Post the ask in this campaign: the campaign's protocol id (`did:ixo:entity:…`, from create_campaign). The deed is classed under it and partOf it, and checked against the campaign's shared requirements. Needs the IXO ask shape.

check.description: With `checker`, when it offers several checks: which one, by name (or its `did`).

checker.description: Have a verifier check the answers by its own rules: its name from `list_checkers` (or its `did`). Its fee per check is the review fee.

confirm.description: The exact total from the preview, e.g. '$1.50'. Omit to preview.

image.description: The ask's picture (png, jpg or webp, at most 5 MB): a file path on this machine, an https URL or a data: URL. Stored on the gateway and set as the deed's profile image. Needs the IXO ask shape.

invite.description: With access "invite" (or "apply", to let some in at once): ixo1 addresses, @handles of people with a page, and "link" once per single-use link you want (each admits one new person).

near.description: Where the work must be done, as "lat,lon", when it has to be done somewhere. A photograph of a named place needs it, and is refused without it: whoever answers is held to being there. E.g. "46.0512,14.5060".

network.description: Which deployment: `mainnet` is the real network (real money); `testnet` is the sandbox (play money, a dry run).

oracle.description: With org: the verifier that judges the ask. With url, its published price is the evaluation payment, in the network's verifier-fee coin, shown as dollars, paid by the organisation's account, which must hold it; without url (your own verifier) the evaluation payment is 0. address: a `did:ixo:entity` verifier's signing account is read from the public record (its #orz), so leave it out; if given it must match. A `did:web` verifier needs it. Omitted: the Asks verifier (this network's own) checks it; for an org, one its settings allow.

org.description: Post for this organisation: its id (`did:ixo:entity:…`). The ask is a deed the organisation requests (linked both ways); you need a key on the organisation, and to own it when the ask holds money: the organisation's account funds the deed (pay x quota in the network's reward coin, shown as dollars, plus the review fee), never this key's account. Needs the IXO ask shape on this deployment.

pay.description: What one approved answer earns, in dollars. 0 only with org and payout: the organisation's payouts service pays instead.

pay_by.description: "card": spend nothing from this key. The Ask is saved and you get a link where the person pays by card and posts it from their own account. Cannot be combined with organisation funding (`org`), custom checks (`oracle`), external payouts (`payout`), a campaign (`campaign`) or an image (`image`). The only way to post from the hosted server.

pay_on_reject.description: Dollars paid to each person whose answer is turned down, so trying is never a total loss. Locked now for every place. Not with pay_by "card", org or payout.

pay_on_submit.description: Dollars paid to each person the moment they send an answer, good or bad, on top of pay. A thank-you for trying. Locked now for every place. Not with pay_by "card", org or payout.

payout.description: With org: pay the worker through the organisation's payouts service (`did:web` or https URL), not from the ask. pay must be 0.

person_checks.description: With approver: up to 5 Yes/No questions for that person (200 characters each). Any No turns the answer down.

place.description: A name for near, shown to whoever answers and frozen into the ask. Only a label: it is never looked up.

plain_key.description: With real money and not connected: spend this key's own money as itself. Without it, a key nobody connected is refused with real money: connect the person's account first (get_connect_link, then connect_account), so it posts as them. The sandbox never needs it.

report.description: With approver, and not for a photo: answers come as a short report with screenshots (or a PDF). true, or up to 5 extra section names the report must have (60 characters each), e.g. ["ISO 29119 checklist"].

series.description: Posting the same job many times, one per address? Give every one the same series name (lowercase letters, digits, dashes) and the board shows them as one card. Each is still its own ask and pays on its own.

task.description: The task, in your own words: everything whoever answers must do. Shown in full on the ask page.

title.description: A short name for the ask, shown as the board card's and the ask page's heading: one plain question or phrase, at most 80 characters, e.g. "Is Red Harbor Ketchup on the shelf at Pick n Pay?". Default: the first sentence of the task, cut to 80 characters.

within_m.description: How close to near, in metres. Default 400.

name: post_ask
title: Post an ask (spends money)
